Marche Easter Cheese Bread

Tall Marche Easter bread enriched with eggs, Pecorino, Grana, butter, and a lightly sweet finish.

Yield: 1 tall loaf, 4–6 servings

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose or strong bread flour
5 medium eggs
1 1/2 cups finely grated Pecorino
1 cup finely grated Grana
7 tbsp softened butter
1/2 cup sugar
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp warm whole milk
about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tsp butter for the pan

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with 2 teaspoons of the sugar.

2. Rest for 10 minutes.

3. Put the flour in a large bowl.

4. Lightly beat the eggs.

5. Add them to the center of the flour.

6. Add the yeast milk and remaining sugar.

7. Knead for 5 minutes.

8. Gradually work in the softened butter.

9. Gradually add the Pecorino and Grana.

10. Add the lemon zest, salt, and pepper.

11. Knead for another 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

12. Cover and rise for about 2 hours, or until doubled.

13. Butter an 8–9-inch tall-sided baking mold.

14. Gently deflate the dough and shape into a ball.

15. Put it in the mold, filling it no more than halfway.

16. Cover.

17. Rise again until the dough nearly reaches the rim.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

19. Bake for 45–50 minutes.

20. If the top browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil during the final 10–15 minutes.

21. Rest in the mold for 10 minutes.

22. Unmold and cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

Add the cheeses after the dough has begun developing structure so their fat and salt interfere less with gluten development.

Solina Bread

Abruzzo naturally leavened loaf made with ancient Solina wheat flour.

Yield: 1 loaf

Ingredients

about 3/4 cup refreshed sourdough starter
1 1/2 cups plus 1 tbsp water
5 cups Solina wheat flour
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp durum semolina for the work surface and pan

Preparation

1. Put the refreshed starter and water in the mixer bowl.

2. Whisk until the starter is well dispersed and slightly foamy.

3. Switch to the dough hook.

4. Add the Solina flour and salt.

5. Mix on low speed.

6. After 3–4 minutes, gradually add the olive oil.

7. Continue kneading for 10–15 minutes.

8. Dust the work surface with half of the semolina.

9. Turn out the dough and work it briefly.

10. Put it in a bowl.

11. Cover with a damp kitchen towel.

12. Rest at room temperature for 1–2 hours.

13. Cover securely and refrigerate for about 18 hours.

14. Return to room temperature for 2 hours.

15. Dust the work surface with the remaining semolina.

16. Shape gently into a loaf without aggressively deflating the dough.

17. Cover and complete the final rise for about 1 hour.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F.

19. Score the loaf.

20. Bake at 480°F for 15 minutes.

21. Reduce the oven to 410–425°F.

22. Bake for about 30 minutes more, until the crust is well developed.

23. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

Solina develops a less elastic gluten network than modern wheat, so shape gently rather than trying to force a highly open crumb.

Pizza Scima

Abruzzo unleavened flatbread made with dry white wine and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: one 9–10-inch flatbread, 4 servings

Ingredients

2 3/4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine, room temperature
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the top
1/2 tsp coarse salt for the top

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a bowl.

2. Add half of the wine, half of the olive oil, and the fine salt.

3. Begin kneading.

4. Gradually add the remaining wine and olive oil.

5. Knead for about 10 minutes, until smooth and uniform.

6. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F.

7. Roll into a disk about 3/8–5/8 inch thick.

8. Place in a parchment-lined 9–10-inch pan.

9. Score deep diamond shapes across the surface without cutting all the way through.

10. Brush with the measured topping oil.

11. Sprinkle with the coarse salt.

12. Bake for about 30 minutes, until golden and crisp.

13. Cool for 5 minutes.

Service

Break along the scored lines and serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Thickness is critical. Because there is no yeast, an overly thick pizza would remain heavy rather than crisp.

Senatore Cappelli Sourdough Bread

Naturally leavened bread made with Senatore Cappelli durum wheat and a long cold fermentation.

Yield: 2 loaves

Ingredients

5 cups Senatore Cappelli durum wheat flour
2 cups plus 3 tbsp water
about 1 cup refreshed sourdough starter
2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the sourdough starter and let it double.

2. Put all of the flour and water in a bowl.

3. Mix only until no dry flour remains.

4. Cover and autolyse for 1 hour.

5. Add the starter in pieces.

6. Knead until evenly incorporated.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Add the salt with lightly damp hands.

9. Knead until fully absorbed.

10. Rest for another 30 minutes.

11. Perform one complete set of stretch-and-folds in the bowl.

12. Cover.

13. Refrigerate at about 45°F for 10 hours.

14. Divide the dough into two equal pieces.

15. Shape gently into two loaves.

16. Put them in floured proofing baskets.

17. Cover.

18. Refrigerate for 12 hours.

19. Put a covered Dutch oven in the oven.

20. Preheat to 445°F for at least 30 minutes.

21. Turn one loaf onto parchment.

22. Score with a sharp blade.

23. Transfer to the hot Dutch oven.

24. Cover.

25. Bake for 30 minutes at 445°F.

26. Remove the lid.

27. Reduce the oven to 410°F.

28. Bake for another 20 minutes.

29. Repeat with the second loaf.

30. Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before slicing.

Chef's note

The high hydration is intentional. Do not add extra flour during handling, because doing so would change the intended crumb structure.

Abruzzo Easter Sweet Bread

Teramo-style Easter bread with long natural fermentation, anise, raisins, candied fruit, lemon, cinnamon, and dark chocolate.

Yield: 1 large Easter bread, about 12 servings

Ingredients

5 cups all-purpose flour
6 large eggs
2 egg whites
1 1/4 cups sugar
about 3 1/3 cups mature sourdough starter
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 tbsp anise seeds
1/3 cup raisins
1/3 cup diced candied citron
1/3 cup diced candied cherries
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1 tsp ground cinnamon
about 2/3 cup chopped dark chocolate
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the mold

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and dry very thoroughly.

3. Beat the 6 eggs with the sugar until pale and foamy.

4. Separately beat the 2 egg whites to soft peaks.

5. Fold the egg whites into the egg mixture.

6. Add the mature sourdough starter and olive oil.

7. Mix until the starter is evenly distributed.

8. Gradually add the flour.

9. Work until the dough is very soft but not liquid.

10. Cover with a clean cloth.

11. Rise in a warm place for about 24 hours.

12. Add the anise seeds, raisins, citron, candied cherries, lemon zest, cinnamon, and chocolate.

13. Knead gently until evenly distributed.

14. Grease a tall baking mold with the measured olive oil.

15. Transfer the dough to the mold.

16. Cover.

17. Rise again for about 19–20 hours.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

19. Bake for about 1 hour, until golden and fully baked through the center.

20. Cool in the mold for 15 minutes.

21. Unmold and cool completely on a rack.

Service

Serve cold, cut into slices.

Chef's note

This traditional bread relies on a very long fermentation. Use a mature, vigorous sourdough starter strong enough to lift a dough rich in eggs and sugar.

Abruzzo Parrozzo

Dome-shaped Abruzzo almond cake covered completely in dark chocolate.

Yield: 6–8 servings

Ingredients

6 tbsp butter, melted, plus 2 tsp softened butter for the mold
2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder for the mold
3/4 cup blanched almonds
1/2 cup cornstarch
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
5 large eggs, separated
1 tsp vanilla extract
2/3 cup sugar
about 1 1/4 cups chopped dark chocolate

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Butter a dome mold with the softened butter.

3. Coat it evenly with cocoa powder.

4. Finely grind the almonds.

5. Sift together the flour and cornstarch.

6. Beat the egg yolks with the vanilla and sugar until pale and very fluffy.

7. Mix in the melted butter.

8. Add the ground almonds.

9. Fold in the sifted flour and cornstarch.

10. Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks.

11. Fold them in gently in three additions.

12. Pour into the prepared mold.

13. Bake for about 40 minutes.

14. Test the center with a skewer.

15. Cool in the mold for 15 minutes.

16. Unmold onto a rack.

17. Cool completely.

18. Melt the chocolate over a water bath or in short microwave intervals.

19. Cool it for 3–5 minutes.

20. Pour over the dome, completely coating the top and sides.

21. Let the coating set at room temperature.

Chef's note

The beaten egg whites provide the cake's primary aeration, so gentle folding matters more than prolonged mixing.

Molise Country Bread

Large naturally leavened Molise loaves with a thick crust and elastic crumb.

Yield: 2 loaves

Ingredients

8 cups plus 1/3 cup type 0, type 2, or bread flour
3 cups water, divided
about 1 2/3 cups refreshed active sourdough starter
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup flour for dusting the work surface and baskets

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a large bowl.

2. Add the refreshed sourdough starter.

3. Add 2 1/2 cups of the water.

4. Mix until no dry flour remains.

5. Knead for 5 minutes.

6. Dissolve the salt in the remaining scant 1/2 cup water.

7. Gradually work the salted water into the dough.

8. Knead for another 8–10 minutes, until smooth, elastic, and well developed.

9. Cover with a cloth.

10. Rise at room temperature for 4–8 hours, until visibly expanded.

11. Dust the work surface with half of the measured flour.

12. Divide the dough into two pieces.

13. Shape into two large round loaves or bâtards.

14. Flour two proofing baskets or towel-lined bowls.

15. Put the loaves seam-side up in the baskets.

16. Cover.

17. Rise for another 2–3 hours.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F with a baking stone or heavy baking sheet.

19. Turn the loaves onto parchment.

20. Score the surfaces.

21. Bake at 480°F for 20 minutes.

22. Reduce the oven to 410°F.

23. Bake for another 30–35 minutes, until the crust is thick and deep golden brown.

24. Cool completely on racks.

Service

Store wrapped in a cotton or linen cloth at room temperature.

Chef's note

Long sourdough fermentation develops the light acidity and durable crust that let this bread keep well for several days.

Molise Cornmeal Flatbread

Molise cornmeal and wheat flatbread served with sautéed field greens.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the flatbread
3 cups fine cornmeal
1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
1 2/3 cups hot water
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the pan

For serving
about 10 cups mixed field greens
2 garlic cloves
1 chile
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

2. Put the cornmeal in a large bowl.

3. Gradually add the hot water while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.

4. Add the wheat flour.

5. Add the salt and 3 tablespoons olive oil.

6. Mix until a thick uniform dough forms.

7. Grease a baking pan with the 2 tablespoons olive oil.

8. Press the dough into a low even disk.

9. Bake at 425°F for 30–40 minutes, until golden on top with a crust underneath.

10. Meanwhile, wash the greens.

11. Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.

12. Boil the greens until tender, about 8–12 minutes.

13. Drain and squeeze dry.

14. Heat the 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.

15. Add the garlic and chile.

16. Cook for 1 minute.

17. Add the greens.

18. Season with salt.

19. Sauté for 5–7 minutes.

Service

Cut the cornmeal flatbread into wedges and serve hot with the sautéed greens.

Chef's note

Use hot water when it meets the cornmeal. This initial scald helps hydrate the corn and makes the dough more cohesive.

Emilia-style yeasted dough made with milk and lard, fried until puffed and golden.

5. Add the flour.

6. Add the softened lard.

Biga Friulana

Paired Friulian rolls made with a long-fermented biga, white spelt, and lard.

Yield: about 10 paired rolls

Ingredients

For the biga
2 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
1/2 cup water
3/4 tsp fresh yeast

For the final dough
all of the biga
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp white spelt flour
1 1/4 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp water, divided
1 tsp barley malt
2 tsp fine salt
3 1/2 tbsp softened lard
2 tbsp flour for dusting

Preparation

1. Mix the flour, water, and yeast for the biga until rough and shaggy.

2. Cover.

3. Ferment for 18 hours at about 64°F.

4. The next day, put the biga in a mixer.

5. Add the spelt, type 0 flour, malt, and about 2/3 cup water.

6. Knead until the dough begins becoming elastic.

7. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 2 tablespoons water.

8. Gradually add the salted water.

9. Work in the lard little by little.

10. Knead until smooth.

11. Cover.

12. Rise for 2 hours.

13. Divide into portions of about 1/2–3/4 cup each.

14. Fold the edges of each portion toward the center.

15. Turn over and shape into smooth balls.

16. Place the balls together in pairs on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Cover.

18. Rise for another 2 hours.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 465°F.

20. Score the rolls with a razor.

21. Dust lightly with the measured flour.

22. Bake for 40 minutes.

23. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

The biga develops flavor and structure during a cool fermentation; do not speed up the 18-hour maturation with higher temperatures.
